title: One Operator, Many Drones: Inside Skydio's Autonomy Stack — Suchet Bargoti, Skydio
talk_summary: Skydio's autonomy lead demos a fleet of docked drones commanded at a high level by cloud agents, with edge autonomy for immediate reactions and cloud-side heavier reasoning. The transferable core is a layered architecture: cheap fast on-device loops, slower cloud models for planning, shared world/map state synced across the fleet, and tool APIs the agent calls instead of hardcoded branching logic.

takeaways.what_they_do: Immediate reactive control runs on the drone; slower, heavier reasoning (VLMs at 1-2s latency) runs in the cloud and only makes broad decisions.
takeaways.numbers: cloud VLM feedback at 1-2 second latency vs 7-10 Hz on-device

takeaways.technique: Shared world model synced across fleet
takeaways.what_they_do: All drones plan against one map; when one drone observes something new (construction site), it feeds back and the whole fleet gets the updated map next iteration.
takeaways.evidence_quote: they're now observing these things that we can feed back into our uh map syncing process ... all the drones in the fleet have this most updated map

takeaways.technique: High-level tools instead of hardcoded branching
takeaways.what_they_do: They expose drone APIs as primitives/tools the agent calls, replacing if/else search-and-rescue logic with high-level commands.
takeaways.evidence_quote: We're trying to get away from having to have all these if statements and the code and these branching strategies and kind of let the agent have some highle tools

takeaways.what_they_do: Every flight logs what was instructed vs what happened, feeding retraining/eval of the autonomy stack.
takeaways.evidence_quote: every single time we instructed this but the drone did this ... That can come back to our uh learning agents ... to retrain, evaluate, and send it back out there

takeaways.what_they_do: They avoid fully end-to-end learned control where reliability/observability matter, keeping hand-engineered segments where debugging is hard.
takeaways.evidence_quote: the observability of what's going wrong and the guarantees on reliability is very difficult today

takeaways.what_they_do: They invest in compressing/encoding data sent to cloud so cloud-side agents get usable input under constrained network.
takeaways.evidence_quote: optimize that being able to un uh um encode that information into smaller sizes and be able to decode into something clear
